name: Satoshi Nakamoto
milestone_by_age_26: No verifiable personal milestone by age 26; Bitcoin was created in 2008 when Nakamoto would have been approximately 33, and the claimed 1975 birth year is likely a pseudonymous political reference rather than a real date of birth.
early_history_summary: Satoshi Nakamoto is a pseudonymous person or group whose true identity has never been verified. The claimed birth date of 5 April 1975 is widely considered a political reference (to US Executive Order 6102) rather than a real birthday. Bitcoin's white paper was published in October 2008 and the network launched in January 2009.
family_context_summary: Not documented — identity is unknown and pseudonymous.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented — identity is unknown and pseudonymous.
evidence_summary: Satoshi Nakamoto is a pseudonymous entity whose real identity, birth year, and personal history are unknown. The claimed 1975 birth year is widely regarded as a political reference rather than a factual date. Bitcoin was created in 2008-2009, which would place the milestone at approximately age 33 if the birth year were accurate. No verifiable personal milestone by age 26 can be identified for an anonymous person.

name: Lars Christiansen
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Danish handball championship with KIF Kolding in 1993 at age 21, and again in 1994, establishing himself as a top Danish player before moving to the German Bundesliga.
early_history_summary: Christiansen began playing handball at Vidar Sønderborg as a youth from 1976 to 1990, then started his senior career at Ribe HK (1990-1992). He moved to KIF Kolding in 1992 and quickly became a Danish champion and cup winner in 1993 and 1994. He debuted for the Denmark national team in 1992 at age 20 and joined SG Flensburg-Handewitt in 1996, where he spent 14 seasons.
family_context_summary: Born in Sønderborg, Denmark, near the German border. Family background not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: early specialization, youth club, border town, national team pipeline
evidence_summary: Christiansen started handball at age 4 at Vidar Sønderborg and spent 14 years in the youth system before turning senior at 18. By 1992 he was in the Danish national team pipeline and won Danish championships with KIF Kolding at ages 21-22. His early immersion in the sport from a very young age in a handball-strong nation provided deep domain proximity and sustained reps. No family background or financial advantage is documented.
starting_point: Born in Sønderborg, Denmark, a town near the German border; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Sport director at KIF Kolding; retired from professional handball in 2012 after a 20-year senior career with 338 national team caps and 1503 goals for Denmark.

name: Irene Sáez
milestone_by_age_26: Won Miss Universe 1981 at age 19, becoming the second Venezuelan to hold the title, after winning Miss Venezuela 1981 earlier that year.
early_history_summary: Sáez was born in Chacao, Venezuela, and orphaned early — her mother died when she was three and her father when she was ten. She was raised by her eldest sister. She was named Queen of Club Campestre Los Cortijos for three consecutive years before winning Miss Venezuela and Miss Universe in 1981 at age 19.
family_context_summary: Born to Carlos Sáez and Ligia Conde in Chacao, Miranda, Venezuela. Her mother died of cancer when she was three and her father died when she was ten; she was raised by her eldest sister.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. Parents were not known to be in pageantry or public life.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Venezuelan pageant system, orphaned early, Club Campestre Los Cortijos, Miss Venezuela pipeline
evidence_summary: Sáez was orphaned by age ten and raised by her eldest sister in Chacao, Venezuela. She gained early visibility through the Club Campestre Los Cortijos pageant circuit before entering the Venezuelan national pageant pipeline, which is one of the world's most competitive. Winning Miss Universe at 19 required physical presence, poise, and access to the Venezuelan pageant ecosystem. No family financial or domain advantage is documented; her adversity as an orphan may have created urgency.
starting_point: Born in Chacao, Miranda, Venezuela to Carlos Sáez and Ligia Conde; orphaned by age ten (mother died at age 3, father at age 10) and raised by her eldest sister.
current_position: Retired from public life; reportedly living in Miami since 2000; former governor of Nueva Esparta and former presidential candidate.

trajectory.event: Won Miss Venezuela 1981 and then Miss Universe 1981 in New York City.

name: Jane Luu
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; the co-discovery of the first Kuiper Belt object occurred in 1992 when Luu was 29, and her PhD was awarded in 1990 at age 27.
early_history_summary: Luu fled Vietnam as a refugee in 1975, settled in Kentucky, and graduated high school as valedictorian. She earned a physics degree from Stanford in 1984, worked at JPL in 1985, and began graduate studies at MIT in 1986. She started the Kuiper Belt survey with David Jewitt in 1987 but the discovery came in 1992.
family_context_summary: Born in Saigon, Vietnam; father was an interpreter for the U.S. Army during the Vietnam War. Family fled as refugees in 1975 and settled in Kentucky with relatives.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was an interpreter for the U.S. Army; no scientific or academic domain background documented.
evidence_summary: Luu was a Vietnamese refugee who excelled academically in the U.S., earning a Stanford physics degree in 1984 and starting at MIT in 1986. She began the Kuiper Belt survey in 1987 as a first-year graduate student, but the first discovery came in 1992 at age 29. Her PhD was awarded in 1990 at age 27. No material, independently verifiable milestone occurred by age 26.

name: Aleksandar Đorđević
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Yugoslav League championship with Partizan Belgrade in 1987 at age 20, and later won the EuroLeague title with Partizan in 1992 at age 25, hitting the championship-winning three-pointer.
early_history_summary: Born into a basketball family in Belgrade — his father Bratislav was a professional basketball player and coach who led Crvena zvezda to the Yugoslav League title in 1972. Aleksandar joined Partizan Belgrade at age 16 in 1983, was immersed in basketball from childhood, and became a key player for Partizan through the late 1980s, winning the Yugoslav League in 1987 and the Korać Cup in 1989.
family_context_summary: Born into a sporting family in Belgrade; both parents were primary school physical education teachers. His father Bratislav was a retired basketball player who became a prominent coach, leading Crvena zvezda to the Yugoslav League title in 1972.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father Bratislav 'Bata' Đorđević was a professional basketball player and later head coach of Crvena zvezda, providing deep basketball domain immersion from birth. Mother Milijana was also a PE teacher.
primary_early_advantage_tags: basketball family, father coach, Partizan Belgrade, Yugoslav basketball system, early immersion
evidence_summary: Đorđević was born into a basketball family in Belgrade where his father was a professional player and prominent coach. He was immersed in the sport from early childhood, joining Partizan at 16 and winning the Yugoslav League at 20 and the EuroLeague at 25. His father's coaching career provided direct domain knowledge, access to elite players, and deep basketball culture immersion. The Yugoslav basketball system was one of the world's strongest development pipelines.
starting_point: Born in Belgrade, SR Serbia, Yugoslavia into a basketball family; father Bratislav was a professional basketball player and coach, mother Milijana a PE teacher; family lived in New Belgrade.
current_position: Head coach of Bahçeşehir Koleji in the Turkish Basketbol Süper Ligi and EuroCup; formerly head coach of the Serbian and Chinese national teams.

trajectory.event: Won the Yugoslav League championship with Partizan Belgrade.

Won the FIBA EuroStar and was named EuroBasket MVP with the Yugoslav national team.
Won the FIBA Champions League as head coach of Segafredo Virtus Bologna.

name: Carlos Queiroz
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; Queiroz played as a goalkeeper at Ferroviário de Nampula in Mozambique during the 1970s but had no notable playing achievements, and his coaching career began in the early 1980s with his first major success coming at the 1989 FIFA World Youth Championship at age 36.

name: Banksy
milestone_by_age_26: No material, independently verifiable milestone by age 26; Banksy's first known large wall mural (The Mild Mild West) was painted in 1997 when he was approximately 27, and his identity remains unconfirmed.
early_history_summary: Banksy is a pseudonymous England-based street artist believed to have been born in the early 1970s in Bristol. He started as a freehand graffiti artist in 1990-1994 as part of Bristol's DryBreadZ Crew. By the mid-1990s he was producing stenciled works around Bristol but had not achieved notable recognition. His first large wall mural was The Mild Mild West in 1997.
family_context_summary: Not documented — Banksy's identity has never been publicly confirmed. Believed to be from Bristol, England.
evidence_summary: Banksy is a pseudonymous artist whose identity has never been confirmed. He began freehand graffiti in Bristol in the early 1990s and transitioned to stencils around 1995-1997. His first known large wall mural, The Mild Mild West, was painted in 1997 when he was approximately 27. No material, independently verifiable milestone occurred by age 26, and his birth year of 1970 is itself unconfirmed.

name: Gennady Rozhdestvensky
milestone_by_age_26: Conducted Tchaikovsky's The Nutcracker ballet at the Bolshoi Theatre at age 20 in 1951, and served as assistant conductor at the Bolshoi from 1951 to 1961, establishing his reputation as one of the youngest conductors at the premier Soviet opera house.
early_history_summary: Born in Moscow to conductor Nikolai Anosov and soprano Natalya Rozhdestvenskaya, Rozhdestvensky studied conducting with his father at the Moscow Conservatory and piano with Lev Oborin. He adopted his mother's maiden name professionally to avoid nepotism. He conducted The Nutcracker at the Bolshoi at age 20 and became assistant conductor there from 1951.
family_context_summary: Born in Moscow to conductor and pedagogue Nikolai Anosov and soprano Natalya Rozhdestvenskaya. He adopted his mother's maiden name professionally to avoid the appearance of nepotism.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father Nikolai Anosov was a conductor and pedagogue at the Moscow Conservatory who taught Rozhdestvensky conducting directly. Mother Natalya Rozhdestvenskaya was a soprano. Both parents were deeply embedded in Soviet classical music.
primary_early_advantage_tags: conductor father, Moscow Conservatory, Bolshoi Theatre, musical family, nepotism avoidance
evidence_summary: Rozhdestvensky was born into a elite Soviet musical family — his father was a conductor and pedagogue at the Moscow Conservatory, his mother a soprano. He studied conducting directly with his father and piano with Lev Oborin, giving him access to the highest level of musical training from childhood. He conducted at the Bolshoi Theatre at age 20, an extraordinary achievement facilitated by his family's position in the Soviet musical establishment, though he adopted his mother's name to mitigate nepotism perceptions.
starting_point: Born in Moscow to conductor Nikolai Anosov and soprano Natalya Rozhdestvenskaya; raised in an elite Soviet musical household with direct access to the Moscow Conservatory and Bolshoi Theatre ecosystem.
current_position: Died on June 16, 2018 in Moscow at age 87; final role was general artistic director of the Bolshoi Theatre (2000-2001) and active conductor until late in life.

trajectory.event: Conducted Tchaikovsky's The Nutcracker at the Bolshoi Theatre and became assistant conductor there.

name: Gary Player
milestone_by_age_26: Won the South African Open in 1956 at age 21 and the British Open (Open Championship) in 1959 at age 23, his first major championship; by age 26 he had accumulated numerous professional tournament wins worldwide.
early_history_summary: Born in Johannesburg, the youngest of three children, Player's mother died when he was eight and his father worked in a gold mine. He took up golf at 14 when his father bought him clubs, turned professional at 17 in 1953, and quickly won tournaments in South Africa, Europe, and Australia. By 21 he had won the South African Open, and at 23 he won his first major, the British Open.
family_context_summary: Born in Johannesburg, South Africa, the youngest of three children. Father Harry Player was a captain in a gold mine who spent most of his working life underground. Mother Muriel died of cancer when Gary was eight. The family was not wealthy; Player described a difficult, lonely childhood.
parent_family_domain_summary: No family background in golf documented. Father worked in gold mining; mother was a homemaker who died when Player was young.
primary_early_advantage_tags: orphaned early, self-driven, South African golf circuit, fitness obsession, adversity
evidence_summary: Player grew up in difficult circumstances — his mother died when he was eight, his father was largely absent working in gold mines, and he described a lonely childhood where he cooked his own meals. He took up golf at 14, turned pro at 17, and by 21 had won the South African Open. His extraordinary work ethic and fitness regimen were self-created responses to adversity. No family golf domain or financial advantage is documented; his success was driven by relentless self-discipline and early access to the South African golf circuit.
starting_point: Born in Johannesburg, South Africa, the youngest of three children; father was a gold mine captain who worked underground, mother died of cancer when Gary was eight; family was not wealthy and childhood was difficult and lonely.
current_position: Retired professional golfer residing in Jupiter Island, Florida and Plettenberg Bay, South Africa; one of only six golfers to win the career Grand Slam with 9 major championships and 159 professional wins; estimated net worth in the hundreds of millions.

trajectory.event: Turned professional golfer and quickly won several tournaments in South Africa.

Won his last Masters Tournament, coming from seven strokes behind in the final round.
Became the oldest golfer ever to make the cut at the Masters at age 62.

name: Neil Druckmann
milestone_by_age_26: No material individual milestone by age 26; Druckmann was a programming intern and then junior programmer at Naughty Dog working on Jak 3 (2004) and Jak X (2005) at ages 25-26, with his first creative design role coming on Uncharted: Drake's Fortune (2007) at age 28-29.

He landed an internship at Naughty Dog in 2004 and became a programmer on the Jak series before transitioning to design.

early_history_summary: Born in São Paulo, Garcia (known as Ricardinho) started playing volleyball at age 9 on medical recommendation after removal of a benign tumor from his left leg. He debuted for the senior national team in 1997 and won the World Grand Champions Cup gold that year.

name: Zhang Zhilei
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Olympic silver medal in super-heavyweight boxing at the 2008 Beijing Olympics at age 25, becoming the first Asian to win an Olympic medal in the unlimited weight class; also won bronze at the 2007 World Championships at age 24.
early_history_summary: Born in Qianzhangying village, Shenqiu County, Henan Province, China, Zhang was enrolled in a rowing team by his father at age 12 to lose weight, but was redirected to boxing. He won third place at the 2001 National Games of China at age 18, became a sparring partner for the national team in 2002, and progressed through international amateur boxing, winning bronze at the 2007 World Championships and silver at the 2008 Olympics.
family_context_summary: Born in a rural village in Henan Province, China. His father enrolled him in a rowing team at age 12 to encourage weight loss, which led to boxing. No further family background documented.

evidence_summary: Zhang grew up in a rural village in Henan Province and entered boxing through a rowing team at age 12. His exceptional size (eventually 1.98m, 111kg) suited super-heavyweight boxing. He entered the Chinese national team pipeline, winning bronze at the 2007 World Championships and Olympic silver at the 2008 Beijing Olympics at age 25. The Chinese state sports system provided the institutional pipeline. No family athletic domain or financial advantage is documented.
